AUTHOR: Saleh
TITLE: Overcoming annotation bottlenecks in underwater fish segmentation: a robust self-supervised learning approach
REGION: Tropical Australia (DeepFish, training); Australian estuaries (Seagrass, test); YouTube-VOS (web, test)
DATA: DeepFish (training, unlabeled), Seagrass/Luderick dataset (4280 frames) and YouTube-VOS fish videos (130 videos, 4349 frames) for evaluation
V_EV: Sec. 4: 'Performance in extreme conditions like poor lighting, turbidity, or variable water clarity was not extensively tested'
D2: Train on DeepFish; test on Seagrass and YouTube-VOS (separate datasets)
D_EV: Sec. 3.1: 'The feature extractor was trained on DeepFish and evaluated on Seagrass and YouTube-VOS.'
R_EV: Abstract: 'Trained on DeepFish, our model exhibits strong generalization, achieving high segmentation accuracy on the unseen Seagrass and YouTube-VOS datasets'; no in-domain DeepFish results reported
E_EV: Tables 1-2: only 'J&F (Mean), J (Mean), J (Recall), F (Mean), F (Recall)' reported
ARCH: Self-supervised CoaT Transformer encoder + MLP, cross-view consistency and space-time self-training, kNN label propagation from first-frame mask
METR: Jaccard index, Dice coefficient (mean and recall)
NOTE: Text file is arXiv v2 (Feb 2025) of the SIVP paper. Cross-dataset design: trained on DeepFish, evaluated only on Seagrass (field estuary data) and YouTube-VOS (web videos); D1 coded 지역 as closest value for entirely separate dataset/region.
